published_statement: NOT RE-READ AT SOURCE THIS STAGE. As the tree quotes it (qeihps.py:23-30): 'I should mention that the previous analysis was performed for a minimally coupled scalar field. An interesting, semiclassically self-consistent wormhole solution is using nonminimal coupling to the curvature [90]. The throat of the wormhole derived is of Planck length or up to the order 10^2 l_pl, so it is doubtful that it can be considered in the regime of the semiclassical approximation. However, it would be of interest to examine that wormhole solution using one of the QEIs for the nonminimally coupled fields derived in [17,30] to determine its exact validity.' The phrases 'examine that wormhole solution using one of the QEIs for the nonminimally coupled fields', 'semiclassically self-consistent wormhole solution', 'nonminimal coupling to the curvature' and 'of Planck length or up to the order 10^2 l_pl' are corroborated by WebSearch hits on arxiv.org/pdf/2405.05963 and arxiv.org/html/2405.05963v1. It is an EXTRAPOLATION/suggestion, not a theorem: it asserts no result about HPS beyond the regime doubt.

lacked_data: What Kontou (2024) had: HPS's 1997 PRL (a letter; plotted solution r0 ~ 0.02 l_P, quartic example 67 l_P, unprinted 200-300 l_P local solutions promised for a separate publication) and the NMC QEIs FO 2008 / FFKP 2023. What she lacked -- and what anyone still lacks -- is not a measured datum but a construction: a Hadamard state on the HPS background whose <T> is the AHS approximation, a reference two-point function W_0 / omega_0 there, and <:phi^2:> in that state. That lack is exactly what blocks the requested test in the tree (qeihps.py:83-86, 104-108), and supplying it would decide the test, not overturn the request. Her throat-size premise does not rest on any datum that has moved: all quantities are in Planck units (C3-C5). The one place her summary is imprecise ('of Planck length') errs AGAINST semiclassical validity being even more doubtful than she says (0.024 l_P; every (9)-class throat <= 0.030 l_P), and the 67 l_P example's throat curvature is Planckian through f''/(2f) = 1/2 (C5c). Evidence therefore runs against M's hypothesis for THIS result: more data sharpens Kontou's doubt rather than refuting it. What is genuinely missing and could move something: HPS's 200-300 l_P solutions (data unpublished; not found) -- if their throat curvature were sub-Planckian everywhere, the doubt would not extend to them; not checkable here.
grade_evidence: The result as the tree uses it is (a) that Kontou 2024 Sec. 5.2 makes this request and names the non-minimal QEIs [17,30] = FFKP and FO, not Fewster-Smith, and (b) the throat-size remark, echoed as a caveat. (a) could NOT be read at source this stage: alphaXiv quota exhausted on all three tools, and every other host for the paper refused by the egress proxy. It is CORROBORATED, not read: two WebSearch hits on the arXiv copy reproduce the request's key phrase and the throat phrase verbatim, and the tree records a full-text reading (DOCKET 64). The ref-number mapping [17]/[30]/[90] is unconfirmed, and the tree's 'computed' FS exclusion is a record lookup (C1, circular). (b) is CHECKED against HPS, READ from cached text: every throat figure behind Kontou's range re-derives (C2 67.26 l_P, C3 0.02428 l_P, C4 decades) and her regime doubt is borne out and extended (C5b l_P^2|Riem| = 1696 at the plotted throat; C5c Planckian R_tltl even at 67 l_P). The one discrepancy ('of Planck length' against 0.024 l_P) is an imprecision in the source's summary that strengthens the doubt -- a discrepancy, not a refutation, and the tree doesn't inherit it. Nothing contradicts the tree's use and no datum moves. Because the statement itself could not be read here it is OPEN, not flattened to STANDS. If a reading of p. 19 and the bibliography confirms the quote, the evidence points to STANDS.
